intro: Courses, levels, exams, and how to talk about what you find easy or hard.
p.academia.consejo: It is a place with classes, for example for languages. It sounds «a-ka-DE-mya».
p.curso.consejo: It is also the school year: «estoy en segundo curso» is the second year.
p.matrícula.consejo: It has an accent on the i: «ma-TRI-ku-la». «Pagar la matrícula» is getting into the course.
p.apuntarse.consejo: Always with «a»: «me apunto a un curso». It changes with the person: «te apuntas».
p.asignatura.consejo: Maths or history are asignaturas. It sounds «a-sig-na-TU-ra».
p.aprobar.consejo: It changes o to ue: «apruebo», «apruebas». Its opposite is «suspender».
p.suspender.consejo: Its opposite is «aprobar». In some Latin American countries «reprobar» is also used.
p.error.consejo: You say «cometer un error». The «rr» in the middle rolls: «e-RROR».
p.repasar.consejo: «Repaso el vocabulario» is reading it again before the exam.
p.nivel.consejo: The language levels are A1, A2, B1, B2… You say «tengo nivel A2».
p.mejorar.consejo: It comes from «mejor». You say «mejorar el nivel» or «mejorar la pronunciación».
p.me cuesta.consejo: It goes with an infinitive: «me cuesta hablar». It works like «gustar»: the verb does not change with «yo».
p.de memoria.consejo: You say «aprender de memoria». It takes no article.
p.equivocarse.consejo: It goes with «se»: «me equivoco», «te equivocas». It means the same as «cometer un error».
b1.texto:
You **te apuntas a** a course, **pagas la matrícula**, take an exam and **apruebas** or **suspendes**.

To learn to do something: **aprender a** + infinitive: **aprendo a** conducir.

**Me cuesta** + infinitive says something is hard for you: **me cuesta** hablar. The opposite: **me resulta fácil**.

To say the goal you use **para** + infinitive: **para mejorar**, tienes que practicar.

The usual phrases are **cometer un error** and **equivocarse**. Making mistakes is part of learning: **no importa**.

For a language level: **tengo nivel A2**. For a school year: **estoy en segundo curso**.
b2.f0.texto: I have signed up for a Spanish course.
b2.f4.texto: To improve you have to practise every day.
b2.f5.texto: I revise the vocabulary every night.
b2.f6.texto: I learn the verbs by heart.
b2.f7.texto: It doesn't matter if you make mistakes.
b2.f8.texto: You are going to pass the exam.
b4.texto:
These structures are very common when talking about studying:

- **apuntarse a** + noun: **me apunto a un curso**.
- **aprender a** + infinitive: **aprendo a conducir**.
- **me cuesta** + infinitive: **me cuesta hablar**. The verb does not change: it stays singular.
- **para** + infinitive = goal: **para aprobar, repaso cada día**.
- **tener que** + infinitive = obligation: **tienes que practicar**.

Some verbs change their vowel: **aprobar → apruebo**, **costar → cuesta**.
b4.e1.texto: I find it hard to revise the verbs.
b4.e2.texto: To pass, I revise every day.
b5.f0.texto: The language school takes up the first floor of an old building.
b5.f1.texto: The students climb the wooden stairs with their heavy backpacks.
b5.f2.texto: In the classroom, a green board keeps traces of white chalk.
b5.f3.texto: The teacher writes a new verb with big letters.
b5.f4.texto: A murmur of voices repeats the words like a shy choir.
b5.f5.texto: At night, Lucía opens her notebook on the kitchen table.
b5.f6.texto: A small lamp draws a circle of yellow light.
b5.f7.texto: She revises the new words in a low voice.
b5.f8.texto: A small mistake appears on the page and disappears with the eraser.
b5.f9.texto: Little by little, the difficult sentences sound clearer in her head.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Apuntarse en» is not said. This verb takes «a».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «De» shows origin. To sign up you use «a».
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Aprobar» is the opposite: getting a high enough mark.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That's it! Suspender is not getting a high enough mark.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Repasar» is studying again what you have seen.
b7.pregunta: Which verb means not passing an exam?
b8.traduccion: To improve you have to practise
b9.o0.refuerzo: The verb does not agree with «yo» but with the action.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Cuestan» is plural. An infinitive asks for singular.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Correct! An infinitive asks for the verb in the singular.
b9.pregunta: Which form of «costar» follows an infinitive?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! You keep it in your head and say it without reading.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That is the opposite: «de memoria» is without a book.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Willingness does not matter. What counts is not looking at the text.
b10.pregunta: What does learning something «de memoria» mean?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I have to revise».
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Aprender de» is not used with another verb. Here it takes «a».
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! You say «aprender a + infinitive».
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Aprender en» shows place. With a verb you use «a».
b12.pregunta: Which word joins «aprender» with another verb?
p.apuntado.consejo: «apuntarse a» means to sign up for a course. The stress is on «TA».
p.practicar.consejo: The «c» before «a» is hard: «prak-ti-KAR». Practice makes perfect.
p.repaso.consejo: It comes from «repasar». The «s» is clear, and the stress is on «PA».
p.vocabulario.consejo: The «v» sounds like «b». The stress is on «LA», and «io» is a diphthong.
p.aprendo.consejo: From «aprender». The «d» between vowels is soft: «a-PREN-do».
p.verbos.consejo: The «v» sounds like «b» and the stress is on «BER». Verbs show actions.
p.cometer.consejo: The «c» before «o» is «k»: «ko-me-TER». You often hear «cometer un error».
p.errores.consejo: The «rr» in the middle is strong. The stress is on «RRO»: «e-RRO-res».
p.mochilas.consejo: The «ch» sounds like «church». Mochila is a backpack carried by students.
p.pesadas.consejo: It is feminine plural to agree with «mochilas». The opposite is «ligeras».
p.restos.consejo: The «s» is clear and the stress is on «RES». Think of chalk traces on a board.
p.verbo.consejo: The «v» sounds like «b». It is the same word as «verbos» in singular.
p.goma.consejo: Also means rubber. Here it is an eraser. The «g» before «o» is hard.
p.difíciles.consejo: The tilde on «í» marks the stress. The «c» before «i» is «th» in Spain.
p.saberlo.consejo: «lo» refers to the content. The verb «saber» means to know.
p.texto.consejo: The «x» sounds like «ks», so it is «TEKS-to». Think of a written passage.
